faqs.q: How much should a beginner run in a week?
faqs.a: Start with a few short sessions a week, mixing jogging and walking, and build up gradually with rest days in between. The WHO advises adults to get at least 75 minutes of vigorous activity like running, or 150 minutes of moderate activity, each week. If you have a heart condition or other health problem, check with a doctor first.

faqs.q: Is it better to run in the morning or the evening?
faqs.a: The best time is the one you can stick to, as both mornings and evenings bring the same health benefits. In hot Indian summers, early morning or late evening is usually safer to avoid the heat, and on high-pollution days it is wiser to run indoors or reduce your intensity. Drink enough water whenever you run.

faqs.q: Is running bad for your knees?
faqs.a: For most healthy people, regular recreational running is not harmful to the knees when you build up gradually, wear supportive shoes and use good form. Sudden jumps in distance, ignoring pain and running through injuries cause most problems. If you already have a knee problem or pain that does not settle with rest, see a doctor or physiotherapist.

faqs.q: Can running help reduce belly fat?
faqs.a: Running can help reduce belly fat as part of overall fat loss, but you cannot burn fat from one spot alone. It burns calories and improves fitness, and combined with a balanced diet, enough sleep and some strength training, it helps lower total body fat, including around the waist.
